title: The Adventures of Philip Marlowe
paragraphs: The run breaks into several distinct periods: NBC / Van Heflin (June 17, 1947 to September 9, 1947) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], CBS / Gerald Mohr (September 26, 1948 to September 29, 1950) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], CBS summer return (July 7, 1951 to September 15, 1951) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and BBC Chandler adaptations (September 26, 1977 to January 16, 1978) on [[org|org.deepv2.f713a484394d0d32|BBC Radio]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Raymond Chandler (creator and author), [[person|gerald-mohr|Gerald Mohr]] (performer), Norman Macdonnell (producer, director, and composer), Roy Rowan (announcer and performer), Richard Aurandt (music, composer, and conductor), Gene Levitt (writer), and Robert Mitchell (writer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], and [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

The stories often return to murder and homicide, private detective work, blackmail and coercion, missing persons and disappearances, jewelry and valuable objects, and Los Angeles and Southern California.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Raymond Chandler literary origin, Postwar Los Angeles hard-boiled radio context, BBC revival of Chandler novels, and Radio Detectives Marlowe retrospective.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|escape|Escape]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], and [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]].
